title: Problem 1.2
statement_text: Determine the complete set of obstructions for diplanar quartic Eulerian digraphs.
context_text: An Eulerian digraph has in-degree equal to out-degree at every vertex; loops, parallel arcs and digons ($uv,vu$) are allowed, and digraphs need not be connected. An embedding of an Eulerian digraph in a surface is an embedding of the underlying graph in which in- and out-arcs alternate in the rotation at each vertex; a digraph with such an embedding in the plane is diplanar. Quartic Eulerian digraphs are those with in- and out-degree $2$ at every vertex; they are ordered by $H\preceq G$ if $H$ is obtained from $G$ by removing directed cycles, deleting isolated vertices and suppressing vertices of degree $2$ (replacing arcs $uv,vw$ by $uw$). For containment of general Eulerian digraphs embeddability is not hereditary, but the authors show it is hereditary under $\preceq$ for quartic ones, so diplanarity is characterised by its obstructions, the $\preceq$-minimal non-diplanar quartic Eulerian digraphs. Equivalently, the problem is to characterise the directed medial graphs of planar graphs. The authors present all known obstructions (doubled cycles, circulants and Möbius ladders, sporadic examples), reduce obstructions with digons to those without (by splitting vertices and inserting paths of digons), and classify all obstructions containing parallel arcs (anti-digons); it is not known whether their list is complete. They suggest treating next the case of simple underlying graphs, planar or not (using Möbius ladders in the non-planar case), and hope the simple, planar, $3$-connected case is more straightforward.
paper_title: Embedding Quartic Eulerian Digraphs on the Plane
